candidates.statement: Gateway /v1/checkout returns 502 because its downstream call to order POST /v1/orders returns 500. Traces and logs show each checkout 502 paired with an order 500 in the same correlation ID, so the failure originates in the order service, not the gateway.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side telemetry (logs, traces, metrics) is absent, so the specific order-internal fault (e.g. db-pool-exhaustion, redis-timeout) is not established.

report.explanation: Checkout 502s are consistently paired with order-service 500s on POST /v1/orders within the same correlation IDs, establishing the order service as the failing dependency. The precise order-internal root cause is not yet evidenced, so only the bounded http-500 candidate is offered.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for POST /v1/orders 500 responses to identify the internal failure cause
Order service metrics for dependency operations (postgresql, payment, inventory) to distinguish pool exhaustion vs downstream latency
Inventory/redis and payment telemetry to rule out downstream-caused order 500s
